column1: # Purpose: the DAST policy, in ZAP's own rules format (`<plugin id>

column3: <url regex>`; tab separated). ZAP reads it (`-c policy.tsv`) and

column1: #          tools/scripts/security-scan.mjs gates the JSON report with it: a FAIL fails the run, a WARN is reported, an
#          IGNORE is dropped; an OUTOFSCOPE regex (matched from the start of the URL) drops those URLs. A plugin not listed takes its risk: High fails, Medium warns, Low and Informational inform.
#          An IGNORE or a downgrade names the reason on its line. Alert ids: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# Injection and server-side flaws fail whatever risk ZAP gives them (active scans only raise these).
# Transport and headers every Stackra host should send (the edge and @stackra/csp).

column3: Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set (FAIL again when STA-2822 sets it on the registry and static hosts)
Missing Anti-clickjacking Header (FAIL again when STA-2822 sets it on the static host)
Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set

column1: # Informational only: they describe the site, not a weakness.

column3: Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments (a docs site and a package registry are full of the word "user")
Modern Web Application (the scan notes a single-page app)
Storable and Cacheable Content (static assets are meant to be cached at the edge)

column1: # Out of scope, by URL (a regex matched from the start of the URL, as ZAP does).
# Cloudflare's own endpoints on every zone, not our code.
# The docs and the registry's package pages quote SQL on purpose (ADRs, READMEs).
# The brand page's long digit strings (asset hashes) read as a card number; no page of the docs holds personal data.
